newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler faces new probe by securities watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Daimler faces new probe by securities watchdog.

text.p: A German securities trading watchdog said on Friday it would again investigate whether Daimler-Benz AG breached a share trading law by predicting a profit for 1995 in May of that year and later posting a huge loss.
Earlier on Friday, the Stuttgart state prosecutors' office said it had dropped its investigation into top managers at Daimler-Benz AG because it had found no evidence that they misled shareholders.
A spokesman for the Federal Securities Trading Supervisory Authority Office said the office would examine documents handed over by the prosecutors.
The watchdog had already investigated the matter in 1995 but had found no evidence of any breach of rules.
Daimler-Benz said in a statement it was took a "relaxed view" of the new probe.

One shareholder had accused Daimler's chief executive Juergen Schrempp, chief financial officer Manfred Gentz, supervisory board chairman Hilmar Kopper and former chief executive Edzard Reuter of withholding negative information about the group's financial health at an annual general meeting in May 1995.

The management had forecast higher profits for 1995 at the meeting but the company went on to post a loss of 5.7 billion marks ($3.7 billion) for the year -- the biggest ever in Germany history -- linked to restructuring measures at the giant industrial group.
